subject: Skyline renewal — dedicated capacity upgrade scenarios and throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@skyline.ai>, Maria Gonzalez <maria@skyline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Skyline renewal — dedicated capacity upgrade scenarios and throughput guarantees

Hi Alex / Maria,

As we approach the renewal window (term ends 2027-06-30), I wanted to surface a few forecast-driven upgrade scenarios for Skyline's Dedicated pool so we can lock in capacity and pricing before Q3 demand ramps. Attached is a growth model (Q2->Q4) and a short terms doc with reserved-pool options.

Quick summary + ask:
- Forecast: baseline production QPS (end Q1) = 650 requests/minute (peak 1.2k/min); token throughput currently ~1.1M tokens/hour. We expect 2.5–3x token growth by Nov '27 with the new summarization pipeline.
- Recommended starting configurations (provisioned GPUs):
  * Conservative (no immediate uplift): keep 8 GPUs, add 20% burst capacity — risk: higher tail latency on 99th pct
  * Mid: reserve 18 GPUs (mix A100q + H100 variants), autoscale burst to 22 GPUs; target sustained QPS uplift ~2.0x
  * Aggressive: reserve 28 GPUs with guaranteed throughput SLOs for peak windows (recommended if Skyline enables full summarization for all users)

Price/term considerations: we can offer a 12-month reserved pool with a graduated discount at the 18 GPU and 28 GPU tiers. Ben is copied to give exact delta pricing.

Questions for you:
1) Do you expect the summarization rollout to hit all users by Sept? That drives the aggressive scenario.
2) Any hard constraints on burst windows / data residency to call out?

Next step: if you confirm a target tier (mid vs aggressive) we can prepare a term amendment + DocuSign draft this week.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Alex Chen <alex@skyline.ai>

Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline renewal — dedicated capacity upgrade scenarios and throughput guarantees

Thanks Lauren — quick follow-up.

Can you break the recommendation down by model family? We currently run three inference tiers:
- extract-lite (small, short requests)
- synth-512 (mid-size summarization)
- long-summarize (8k+ tokens)

Specifically:
- What GPU mapping (count / class) do you recommend per tier?
- What's the expected 99th-pct latency for each scenario during peak?
- Ballpark monthly delta vs current committed spend if we move to the 18 GPU reserved pool (including the 20% burst option).

Also, Maria is in procurement — looping her on timing questions. We should get procurement sign-off before committing to an expanded capacity.

Appreciate the detail — Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Skyline - capacity sizing + pricing suggestion

Folks — quick internal reply to Alex's ask, consolidated recommendations and pricing posture. Copying Rishi for perf targets and Monica for onboarding/ops notes.

Sizing (recommended mid tier -> targeted offer):
- extract-lite: allocate 2x smaller vGPU instances across 18-GPU pool (effectively 3 dedicated small workers). Expected 99th-pct latency ~120ms under mid tier.
- synth-512: allocate 6 GPUs optimized for throughput (mixed precision quantized); expected 99th-pct ~350–420ms at median peak.
- long-summarize: allocate 10 GPUs (H100/q models prioritized) with KV cache warmers for known prefixes; expected 99th-pct ~850–1,200ms on heavy peaks.

Total: 18 reserved + 20% burst (22) covers expected sustained growth to ~2.1x current QPS. If they choose aggressive, 28 reserved reduces 99th pcts by ~25% and improves headroom for unexpected feature launches.

Pricing delta (ballpark monthly):
- Current committed spend: $126k/mo
- Mid tier (18 GPU reserved + burst): ~$185k/mo (includes 20% reserved discount + fixed monthly baseline for 12-month term)
- Aggressive (28 reserved): ~$265k/mo (larger discount tier; requires 12-mo commitment)

SLA & guarantees: propose a per-route 99th-pct latency target for long-summarize of <1.2s with credits if violated (standard SLA template). Ops can enforce pre-warm policies and scheduled maintenance windows.

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pool_terms_v1.pdf (includes sample SLA language and burst policy).

If everyone agrees, Lauren can send the mid-tier term amendment with the HubSpot deal link and DocuSign draft.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Account Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Skyline renewal — dedicated capacity upgrade scenarios and throughput guarantees

Alex / Maria — thanks for the prompt questions. Per Ben/Rishi's sizing above, here's a clearer per-model breakdown and the expected impact on your spend and latency.

Per-model mapping (mid tier — 18 reserved / 22 burst):
- extract-lite (20% of current traffic): 2 logical small workers -> 2 GPUs equivalent. 99th-pct ~100–140ms.
- synth-512 (45%): 6 GPUs optimized for throughput, token-batching enabled. 99th-pct ~320–450ms.
- long-summarize (35%): 10 H100-class GPUs with longer context pre-warms; 99th-pct ~800–1,150ms depending on token length.

Token growth assumptions baked into the model (attached skyline_q2_q4_growth_model.xlsx):
- Q2->Q4 token/hour growth: scenario median = 2.5x, high = 3.1x if full rollout in Sept.
- Peak concurrency forecast: current 850 concurrent requests -> mid-tier provisioned for 1,900 concurrent peak.

Cost delta (monthly, includes reserved discount / fixed baseline):
- Current: $126k/mo
- Mid tier: $185k/mo (delta +$59k/mo) — includes 12-month term and 10% onboarding credit applied in month 1
- Aggressive: $265k/mo (delta +$139k/mo) — requires net-new PO and 12-month commit

Recommended next steps:
1) If Skyline commits to mid tier by EOD Wed (Apr 14), we will issue a term amendment + DocuSign link with proposed SLA language and a target kickoff week of May 3 for capacity provisioning and smoke tests.
2) Ops (Monica) will run a short warm-up plan and share a calendar for pre-warm windows and KV cache seeding.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/skyline-ai/record) and the DocuSign draft will be attached when you confirm tier.

Lauren
